The story uses restrained, evocative metaphor: “Die Elbe ist der Motor” conveys both the ferry’s mechanics and Ilse’s dependence on the river, while the current taking hold “als hätte der Fluss sich entschieden” gives it agency. The ferry seemingly hanging from nothing in the fog also subtly mirrors the uncertainty beneath Ilse’s dependable routine. These images deepen the atmosphere and characterization without forcing an explicit symbolic reading.
